title: Passenger of suspected car thief shot by police facing her own charges
article: The passenger of a suspected auto thief fatally shot by police this week was in Calgary court Thursday facing her own set of charges.
Duty counsel Joel Livergant asked that Anita Soloway's case be adjourned to Friday so the Crown can review the file.
Prosecutor Tiffany Dwyer told provincial court Judge Gerald Meagher her initial position is the Crown will be asking to detain Soloway.
"At this time the Crown is opposed to her release and we are asking to adjourn to (Friday) to get more information," Dwyer said.
Soloway, 31, faces nine charges from five separate incidents, including an allegation she was breaching her release conditions by being in a motor vehicle without the registered owner.
Police confirmed she was in the car when Terrence Weinmeyer was shot dead by police on Tuesday in the city's northwest.

Weinmeyer, 49, whom police once branded a "high risk" and "prolific" car thief, died in hospital after he was shot in a crowded strip mall parking lot in the 5000 block of 16th Avenue N.W. on Tuesday afternoon.
According to the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, which is investigating the shooting, police officers tried to apprehend a man seen driving a stolen blue Dodge pickup truck.
Among the charges Soloway faces are five allegations from Nov. 2, involving possession of stolen property, narcotics and break and enter tools.
At the time of his death Weinmeyer was on bail for possession of two stolen vehicles, including one from Nov. 2.
